fields.features_heading: Inside a Dog Breed Quiz Built on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: One prompt builds the questions, the results, and the table behind them. Describe a change, and Emergent makes it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions mapped to the breeds you pick

List the breeds you want as results, like Greyhound or Border Collie. Emergent builds the quiz with each option mapped to one breed, and a follow-up prompt changes any question.
fields.feature_2:
Every match saved with its answers

Each finished quiz is a row in a database you own: the breed, each option picked, and an email if the taker gave one. Filter by breed to see which match came up most.
fields.feature_3:
Adoptable dogs on the result screen

Connect your adoption records or store catalog through its API and tag each dog or product by breed. The result screen then lists only the dogs or products with that tag.
fields.feature_4:
An alert for whoever calls back

Send an email or Slack alert when someone finishes, addressed to the breeder, trainer, or adoption coordinator who follows up. It carries the result and every answer.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Takers answer one question per screen, sized for a phone. A quiz shared with a rescue's 18,000 followers records every match, because Emergent puts no cap on responses.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code in GitHub

Run the quiz on your rescue's or shop's own domain, which is included in Emergent and paid in credits. On paid plans, export the quiz's full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Where Dog Breed Quiz Results Go Next
fields.tab_content_1:
Three Greyhounds for adoption on her result screen

Teodora Malkin takes the dog breed quiz on Pinyon Flats Dog Rescue's site and lands on Greyhound. Her result screen lists the 3 adoptable dogs the rescue tagged Greyhound, pulled from its adoption records. Her result and email are saved to the adopter table, and the rescue invites her to meet all 3 on Sunday.
fields.tab_content_2:
Henrike reads every answer ahead of Saturday

Oxbow Bend Labradors sends its quiz to every family asking for a spot on the waitlist. Corbin Tsosie answers on Tuesday: a fenced yard, kids aged 6 and 9, and a dog alone 4 hours on weekdays. His result is Labrador Retriever, and breeder Henrike Vos gets an email with every answer before Saturday's call.
fields.tab_content_3:
Border Collie leads land in a herding class

Thimbleton Dog School sorts each quiz lead by its result. Every Border Collie result goes to Gwendolyn Iturbe, who runs the herding and agility class, and every French Bulldog result goes to Yusra Haldane's city manners class. Mireille Ota lands on Border Collie, and her lead reaches Gwendolyn with every answer.
fields.tab_content_4:
3,600 results and a doubled bed order

This winter, 3,600 shoppers finished Paddock and Leash Supply's quiz. Labrador Retriever led with 1,140, then French Bulldog at 980, Cavalier King Charles Spaniel at 720, Border Collie at 460, and Greyhound at 300. In February the owner saw 1,700 French Bulldog and Cavalier results and doubled the small bed order.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Dog Breed Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a dog breed quiz whose results name a breed and lead to a next step, then build it on Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick five breeds before any question
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about the home, not looks
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 One option per breed, every question
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick five breeds before you write a word of the quiz, and choose ones you would gladly place with a family. Give each breed two lines: the home it suits and the daily exercise it needs. Every question then has somewhere to send each option.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about the home the dog will live in: the yard, the hours everyone is out, and a normal Saturday. Questions about looks pull people toward the breed they already want. Questions about routine sort them toward one that fits.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write one option for each breed in every question, all the same kind and about the same length. If a question has no Greyhound option, nobody who answers it can move toward Greyhound, and that result shows up less than it should.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Stop at eight questions with one question per screen and a progress bar. That is enough to separate five breeds, and short enough that someone finishes it on a phone during a lunch break instead of closing the tab halfway.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Write each result as a lean
fields.howto_step_5_des: Open each result with what the answers point to: your answers lean toward a calm home and short runs. Then name the breed and one honest note on care. Tell people to meet the dog first, since a breed match is a starting point.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Put the next step in your prompt
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide what the result screen hands over: adoptable dogs with that tag, an email to the breeder, or a lead routed to a trainer. Write that into your prompt, and Emergent builds the step along with the quiz and its table.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Play every result once before sharing
fields.howto_step_7_des: Take the quiz five times, once per breed, choosing the options that point to it, and confirm that breed wins. Then open the saved row and any alert it sends before the link goes into a newsletter or onto your adoption page.

faq_plan.q: What is a dog breed quiz?
faq_plan.a: A dog breed quiz is a short set of questions about your home, schedule, and habits, scored so your answers point to one dog breed. The quiz on this page asks eight questions and names one of five breeds, from Labrador Retriever to French Bulldog.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a dog breed quiz?
faq_plan.a: Decide which breeds the quiz can name, then describe the quiz in a prompt, including what the result screen shows. Emergent's AI survey builder drafts each question with one option per breed and saves every finished quiz to a database you own. Publish it and share the link.

faq_plan.q: How does a dog breed for me quiz pick one result?
faq_plan.ref: what dog breed am i quiz
faq_plan.secondary: what dog breed am i quiz
faq_plan.a: It counts which breed your answers point to most often. Each option adds a point to one breed, and the breed with the most points after the last question is your result. If two breeds tie, the quiz needs a rule for which one wins, such as the first breed on its list. A what dog breed am I quiz scores the same way.

faq_plan.q: What should a best dog breed for me quiz ask about my home?
faq_plan.ref: best dog breed for me quiz
faq_plan.secondary: best dog breed for me quiz
faq_plan.a: It should ask about indoor space and the yard, the hours it would spend alone, and how much exercise you can give on a weekday. Weigh those answers above a favorite look. The same idea makes a good style quiz: ask about real choices, not how people see themselves.

faq_plan.q: How many breeds should a dog breed selector quiz include?
faq_plan.a: Five is a workable number for an eight-question quiz. Each question then holds one option per breed without running past a phone screen. Add a breed only when you add a question, and each breed keeps a fair path to win. On Emergent, adding a sixth breed later is one follow-up prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a dog breed personality quiz help a pet brand grow its email list?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the email is optional and the result comes first. Put the offer on the result screen, such as breed care tips by email, and ask for nothing before it. Emergent sets no response caps, and a quiz shared widely records every result.

faq_plan.q: Can an ultimate dog breed quiz mix trivia with breed matching?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as long as the two parts are scored separately. Trivia questions have one right answer and a score, the way a vocabulary quiz does, while matching questions add points to a breed. Put the trivia round last. The breed match then never depends on how many facts someone knows.

faq_plan.q: Should a dog breed quiz ask for an email before showing the result?
faq_plan.a: No. Show the result first and ask for the email after, as an option with a clear reason, like a care checklist for that breed. Keep the email field optional. Nobody should have to sign up to see a match. Each address someone does give lands in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Is a what dog breed are you quiz the same as a genetic breed test?
faq_plan.a: No. A what dog breed are you quiz matches a person to a breed from their answers about home and habits. It says nothing about the ancestry of a dog you already own. Keep the two apart in your copy, and never word a quiz result as if it describes a real dog's breed mix.

faq_plan.q: Where should a pet startup put its dog breed quiz?
faq_plan.a: Give it a page of its own and link that page from the home page and from every social post that mentions the quiz. Look at the best startup landing pages for layout ideas, then put one action above the fold: starting the quiz. Keep the first question visible without scrolling on a phone.

quiz.title: Which Dog Breed Fits Your Home?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about your home, your week, and your weekends. Your result names the breed your answers lean toward, with what to plan for before you meet one.

questions.text: Where would your dog spend most of the day?

options.text: A house with a big fenced yard
A farm or acreage with room to run
A small house, mostly on the couch with you
A quiet home with a soft bed to nap on
A city apartment a block from a park

questions.text: How much exercise can you give a dog on a weekday?

options.text: Two hours of running, training, and games
A gentle walk and plenty of lap time
One fast run, then a long rest
Two short walks around the block
An hour of fetch, swimming, or a long walk
Someone who is home most of the day
Calm adults who like a quiet house
One or two people in a small city place
A busy family with kids and visitors
One or two active adults who like a project

questions.text: What sounds like a good Saturday with your dog?

options.text: A quick sprint in a fenced field, then a nap
A walk to a cafe to watch people go by
A morning at the lake throwing a ball
An agility or herding class
Brunch on a dog-friendly patio

options.text: Short, fun sessions between other things
The basics plus a good retrieve
A new challenge every single week

Happy with a dog that learns at its own pace

questions.text: Which size fits your car and your couch?

options.text: Large and sturdy
Medium and lean
Small enough for a lap
Tall and slim
Small and solid

questions.text: What does a good evening at home look like?

options.text: One more training game before bed
A dog curled up on your lap during a show
A dog stretched out asleep on its own bed
A short stroll to the corner and back
Everyone on the floor playing with the dog

questions.text: Which compliment would you most like to hear about your dog?

options.text: So sweet and gentle
Calm and graceful
Funny and full of character
Everyone's best friend
The smartest dog in class

results.title: Labrador Retriever
results.description: Your answers lean toward a big, social dog that joins every family plan. The AKC describes Labs as friendly, outgoing, and high-spirited companions. Plan on daily exercise, a yard or a park close by, and room in the car for a large dog.

results.title: Border Collie
results.description: Your answers lean toward a dog that wants a job and a lot of daily activity. The AKC calls the breed a remarkably bright workaholic. Budget time every day for training, games, or a herding or agility class, or look at a calmer breed.

results.title: Cavalier King Charles Spaniel
results.description: Your answers lean toward a small, affectionate dog that stays close to you. The AKC says Cavaliers combine the gentle attentiveness of a toy breed with the verve of a sporting spaniel. Gentle walks and lap time suit this match.

results.title: Greyhound
results.description: Your answers lean toward a calm home and short runs. The AKC calls the Greyhound a gentle, noble, and sweet-tempered companion with an independent spirit. Plan on a soft bed, a safe fenced space to run, and patience with training.

results.title: French Bulldog
results.description: Your answers lean toward a small, sturdy dog that fits city life. The AKC calls the Frenchie playful, alert, and adaptable, and notes the breed is popular with city dwellers. Short walks and short, fun training sessions fit this match.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is breed selectors (AKC, Iams, Royal Canin, Purina); the page gives a playable 8-question selector with AKC-sourced results, then the builder angle for rescues, breeders, trainers and stores.

specificity.evidence: Rescue and breeder vocabulary: 'adoptable dogs the rescue tagged Greyhound', 'a spot on the waitlist', 'herding and agility class', 'small bed order'.

openers.evidence: Full-sentence openers: 'Teodora Malkin takes the dog breed quiz...', 'Pick five breeds before you write a word of the quiz...'.

craft.evidence: No tacked-on endings; sentence lengths vary.

voice.evidence: Specific: 'If a question has no Greyhound option, nobody who answers it can move toward Greyhound.'

truth.evidence: All five AKC lines match their quoted domain_sources spans; 1,140+980+720+460+300 = 3,600; 980+720 = 1,700; every question has exactly one option per breed, as how-to step 3 says; claims map to approved ids (api-connect for adoption records, alerts, no-caps).

distinct.evidence: Breed tagging of adoptable dogs, waitlist screening and lead routing by result are particular to this page; FAQ 9 separates it from DNA tests.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions answered in the first sentence; hub link in FAQ 2; secondaries used naturally (dog breed for me quiz, best dog breed for me quiz, dog breed selector quiz, dog breed personality quiz, ultimate dog breed quiz, what dog breed are you quiz, what dog breed am i quiz).
